Every year of the world, on one map.

IntMap is a free world map you can set to any date from 123,000 BC to today. Borders, figures and layers follow the clock, and the sources behind them are named.

Open the map See the examples

Free. No account needed to use the map.

What makes it different

One clock for the whole map

Move the clock and the map moves with it: country borders from 54 historical snapshots before 1689, from OpenHistoricalMap from 1689 to 1885, and day by day from CShapes 2.0 from 1886 to 2019 — and the countries panel shows the figures for that year where its source has them.

Honest about what it knows

IntMap has 164 layers, and the Data sources page names every organisation whose data they show. Set the clock to a date a source does not describe and that layer is not drawn — the map tells you so, instead of showing today’s data under an old date.

Ask the map in words

Signed in, you can ask Atlas, IntMap’s AI assistant, in plain language. It answers on the map itself — turning layers on, moving the camera and the clock.

Who it is for

For map and history lovers

Open a year, compare it with another, and share exactly what you see with one link. Every example below opens in one tap, just as pictured.

Browse the examples →

For teachers

Nothing to install and no sign-up for students: a link opens the same map on every device in the room. Each example comes with a question for class.

Japan in 1900

Japan divided into prefectures, not the old provinces: the domains were abolished in 1871. Taiwan is under Japanese rule, and Korea is the Korean Empire.

Questions

Is IntMap free?

Yes. The map, every layer and the clock are free to use. Running costs are covered by donations.

Do I need an account?

No. Everything on the map works without one. Signing in adds Atlas, the AI assistant (with a daily limit per account), and keeps your settings in sync.

Where does the data come from?

From the organisations that publish it — weather services, NASA, UN bodies, universities, OpenStreetMap and historical-map projects. Every one is listed with its licence on the Data sources page. Data sources →

How are the calculations done?

What each feature and simulation computes, and under which assumptions, is written out on the Science & logic page. Science & logic →

What about my privacy?

You can use the map without an account. What is stored when you sign in, and which services your browser contacts, is set out in the Privacy Policy. Privacy Policy →

Can I share a map?

Yes. The Share button gives a link that reopens the same position, zoom, base map, layers and date.
